target.title: fix(memory): recover from same-file legacy index divergence
target.body:
Related: #108532

Continues #109865. This supersedes that stalled PR because its contributor branch cannot be updated from this environment. Credit to @Serhii-Leniv for the original fix; the first three commits preserve Serhii Leniv's authorship.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Gateway crash loop when legacy and canonical Memory Core rows live in the same per-agent SQLite database with the same identities but different values. In this state, `openclaw doctor --fix` could exit successfully without repairing the database, and the next Gateway start failed again.

The original issue is closed as #108532, but its [Docker reproduction and doctor evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108532#issuecomment-4987458050) show that this same-file failure remained. This PR preserves that paper trail without reopening the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Same-file migration now keeps canonical rows authoritative, imports safe legacy-only rows, and drops legacy tables only after identity/ownership checks. Chunk migration snapshots source ownership before copying so stale chunks cannot be mixed into a canonical-owned chunk set.

A chunkless canonical source imports legacy chunks only when its source metadata still matches. Divergent chunkless sources are invalidated for normal sync. If a canonical source has some chunks but legacy exposes additional chunk identities, its canonical chunks still win, but its source metadata is invalidated so hash-based sync cannot mistake a partial chunk set for a complete index.

The migration tests were split into `memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts`, keeping both files under max-lines without a suppression or loss of migration-boundary coverage.

### Root Cause

The same-file migration compared complete row values after conflict-ignored inserts. A canonical/legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, or `embedding_cache` row with the same key but different values therefore threw a plain `Error("legacy memory <table> rows conflict with canonical memory index rows")`.

Runtime startup reaches that assertion through Memory Core schema initialization. Doctor reaches it before entering the sidecar recovery block. The #108652 recovery catches `LegacyMemoryDerivedRowsConflictError` from the sidecar import only, so it cannot recover this plain same-file error. Startup refuses readiness; doctor leaves the same conflict in place.

This change validates canonical identity coverage rather than duplicate derived-row values. Rows that cannot be represented by the canonical STRICT schema still fail closed and retain the legacy tables.

## User Impact

Memory Core starts when an older same-file index contains stale values for identities already present canonically. Canonical content wins, safe legacy-only content remains searchable, ambiguous partial sources are marked for rebuild, and repeated schema initialization is idempotent.

Genuinely uncopyable legacy rows—for example, values rejected by canonical STRICT constraints—still hard-fail. That residual case is intentionally unchanged follow-up work.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, isolated session-owned state directories and free loopback ports, real on-disk `DatabaseSync` files in WAL mode. Final rebased base: `1ca26c508db14b141935c8f1c7c71660c8a14273`. Final exact PR head: `60cb875d203d26d6a417084e386de5211c9cdd7c`.

Each fixture placed the affected database at `$STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. That one file held canonical `memory_index_*` tables plus partially migrated legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, and `embedding_cache` tables. Every legacy table had a same-identity/different-value conflict. It also had a legacy-only `LEGACY_ONLY.md` source/chunk containing the unique term `saffronquasar`, absent from canonical rows. A normal `$STATE_DIR/memory/main.sqlite` sidecar exercised the real startup/doctor state-migration path.

This reproduces the important mounted-state constraint: the divergent tables are inside the canonical agent database, so doctor cannot recover by renaming that database aside as a derived sidecar. No Docker daemon, container, bind mount, or OS-level rename denial was used.

#### Current-main failure

The crash reproduction was run on `cc0a977dd5b12f12d56516478f2f97a30b814c1f`. The later base delta through `1ca26c508db14b141935c8f1c7c71660c8a14273` was audited and contained no `memory-core`, `memory-host-sdk`, doctor, agent-DB, or state-migration changes.

Redacted transcript; `$STATE_DIR`, `$PORT`, and fixture paths replace temporary local values.

```text
$ node <proof-fixture> seed <main-case>
{"seeded":true,"journalMode":"wal","partialMigration":true,"memoryStateHash":"9f0ed74b181898f3527a527b2f3ae8d36bd9b567439f6026e5375af45723b152"}

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import for agent main because the sidecar could not be imported: Error: legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
exit=1

$ HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... \
    node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
- Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import for agent main because the sidecar could not be imported: Error: legacy memory meta rows conflict with canonical memory index rows
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0

$ node <proof-fixture> assert-baseline <main-case>
{"baselineStillDiverged":true,"legacyTables":["meta","files","chunks","embedding_cache"],"sidecarPresent":true,"memoryStateHash":"9f0ed74b181898f3527a527b2f3ae8d36bd9b567439f6026e5375af45723b152"}

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
exit=1
```

Gateway failed, doctor exited 0 without changing the memory-row hash, and the next Gateway failed identically.

#### Final exact-head Gateway-first path

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
60cb875d203d26d6a417084e386de5211c9cdd7c

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Migrated Memory Core legacy memory index for agent main -> per-agent SQLite (1 source(s), 1 chunk(s), 1 cache row(s))
- Archived Memory Core legacy memory index sidecar -> $STATE_DIR/memory/main.sqlite.migrated
[gateway] ready

$ curl --silent --show-error --fail --write-out '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/readyz
{"ready":true,"failing":[],...}
HTTP 200

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search saffronquasar --agent main --json
{"results":[{"path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","snippet":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration","score":0.9695528134366842,...}]}

$ node <proof-fixture> check <gateway-case>
{"canonicalWins":true,"legacyOnlyRowsRetained":true,"sameFileLegacyTablesRemovedAfterChecks":true,"ftsSentinel":"LEGACY_ONLY.md:saffronquasar","memoryStateHash":"bf40fc40048ab14310eef86e36cf7abbb2f92ea4958c10cc416975a3fce941f5"}
```

The full Gateway-first matrix was also repeated on the immediately preceding patch-identical rebased head: a clean doctor run, second Gateway readiness, second actual FTS query, and unchanged row-state hash.

#### Final exact-head doctor-first path

A separately seeded fixture proved the repair does not depend on Gateway running first.

```text
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
[state-migrations] Auto-migrated legacy state:
- Migrated Memory Core legacy memory index for agent main -> per-agent SQLite (1 source(s), 1 chunk(s), 1 cache row(s))
- Archived Memory Core legacy memory index sidecar -> $STATE_DIR/memory/main.sqlite.migrated
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search saffronquasar --agent main --json
{"results":[{"path":"LEGACY_ONLY.md","snippet":"legacy-only searchable saffronquasar survives migration","score":0.9695528134366842,...}]}

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port $PORT --bind loopback --auth none
[gateway] ready
$ curl .../readyz
{"ready":true,"failing":[],...}
HTTP 200

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
# no Memory Core legacy-state detection, migration warning, or repair
└  Doctor complete.
exit=0

$ node <proof-fixture> check <doctor-case>
{"canonicalWins":true,"legacyOnlyRowsRetained":true,"sameFileLegacyTablesRemovedAfterChecks":true,"ftsSentinel":"LEGACY_ONLY.md:saffronquasar","memoryStateHash":"bf40fc40048ab14310eef86e36cf7abbb2f92ea4958c10cc416975a3fce941f5"}
```

The real memory search command used the built-in FTS path (`provider: none`, vector disabled), so the searchability assertion did not depend on a mock, a SQL-only assertion, a model download, or a provider credential.

### Verification

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

Tests include an interrupted source with one canonical chunk and an additional legacy identity. Migration keeps the canonical chunk and removes source metadata so normal sync must rebuild rather than accepting an incomplete set.

```text
$ pnpm format packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts
$ git diff --check
$ git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# all clean; no max-lines suppression
```

Fresh branch autoreview found the ambiguous partial-source case above. After the source invalidation fix and regression test:

```text
$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.89)
```

### What was not tested

- No Docker daemon/container or real bind-mounted filesystem was used. The proof exercised the canonical path, WAL mode, partially migrated same-file schema, real Gateway startup/readiness, real `doctor --fix`, real FTS search, and repeated-run idempotence on isolated local state.
- Vector/semantic search was not exercised. The fixture intentionally used credential-free FTS-only search with vector disabled; a vector query would require an embedding provider/model and sqlite-vec setup.
- No packaged install, full test suite, or cross-platform run was performed. The source CLI rebuilt and ran on the exact final head; the touched schema tests and static checks are listed above.
